thread:
maria_g: Thinking out loud — the v3 -> v4 soft-cutover is tight for a few large tenants. Can we stretch the cohort window and stage by traffic profile instead of time?

alex_k: yep. cohort by p50 request size + embed volume. smaller tenants -> full cutover earlier. big ones get longer "stretch" window.

jonathan_r: we should avoid doubling the complexity in the gateway. Proposal: keep a single header opt-in and central routing table that maps tenant -> cohort. e.g. `X-Cohort: v4-canary` or `X-Compat-Opt-In: v4`

samir: agree on header, + add telemetry flag so we can detect silent failures quickly. what metrics do we need? error-rate, 99th latency, token-regression count?

maria_g: yes to those. also want a tolerance budget: if v4 causes >1.5x latency or token-loss >0.5% for a tenant over 1h, auto-fallback them.

alex_k: rough config sketch for routing table and fallback window:

```
# cohorts.yml
cohorts:
  - name: small
    selector: tenant.qps < 50 && avg_tokens < 512
    window: 24h
  - name: medium
    selector: tenant.qps < 500
    window: 72h
  - name: large
    selector: tenant.qps >= 500
    window: 168h  # stretch window
fallback_policy:
  latency_multiplier: 1.5
  token_regression_pct: 0.5
  evaluation_interval: 1h
```

jonathan_r: +1. We should keep this logic in the control plane (private deployments too) so Dedicated/private customers can opt to use cohorts or not. Means exposing a small API to manage cohort overrides.

samir: obs/alerts: create an aggregate regression alert (per-tenant) and a rollup (cluster-level). Also instrument prefix-cache hit-rate since that changes cost profile.

maria_g: operational notes: owners for waves: @alex_k owns routing changes, @jonathan_r owns control-plane API, @samir owns telemetry & alerts. need runbook for manual rollback and for forced-fallback when probe false-positives occur.

alex_k: testing plan: 1) local simulation (replay traces) 2) small canary tenants (5) with heavy tokens 3) progressive waves by cohort 4) full cutover; each wave gated by the tolerance budget.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by maria_g: `deploy cohort-routing v1.3` — staging started :rocket:

jonathan_r: one more open question — do we want a short-lived compatibility shim at the runtime to translate a few legacy fields, or rely fully on the gateway? Shims reduce client pain but add runtime complexity.

maria_g: leaning to gateway-only, + a small shim library we can drop into private deployments (opt-in). avoids runtime perf tax in hosted path.

samir: ok. add a telemetry tag when shim is used so we can measure usage and eventual removal.

alex_k: I'll PR the cohort selector RFC and include the config example + rollout playbook. Plan to start canary next Tue morning.

maria_g: thanks all. I'll draft the rollback runbook and post in #release-war-room. We should sync Wed to confirm canary list. :thumbsup:

jonathan_r: acked. I'll add a minimal control-plane API swagger and post link.

samir: will create the dashboard & alerts in Datadog, include migration-specific widgets.

maria_g: perfect. closing the thread — owners assigned, canary date set, fallback rules in config.
